claims: `terraform test` fails — the required PR gate cannot pass: `alerts/rules/peg-rule-definitions.tftest.hcl:68-69` assertion requires `peg_slack_title` to contain `$alert.Annotations.summary` and `$alert.Annotations.resolved_summary`, but `peg-message-templates.tf:13-17` removed both; the Terraform sibling test was not updated

A recovered rule shows "Monitoring failed" forever — `peg-alert-events.ts:105-115`, `route.ts:43-56`: the `Error → Pending` row is neither fetched by `errorStateHistoryUrl` nor classified (`transitionKind` returns `null` when `current` is `Pending`), so the error cycle opened at `Normal → Error` never closes and `pairStateTransitions:356` flushes it as a permanently-unresolved event

Incidents that start from an Error lose "lasted X" on resolution — `peg-alert-events.ts:320-321` (with `:109-110`): `cycleKey` routes any kind starting with `"error"` to the `error` cycle, so `Error → Alerting` never opens the alert cycle and the later `Alerting → Normal` falls through to `unpairedCleared` and is emitted with no duration

Two supplementary queries are now hard dependencies of the whole panel — `route.ts:63-83`: four upstream calls inside a `Promise.all` that rejects on first failure, so if the new error-history queries fail or time out the entire seven-day peg alert history disappears; it should fail open

Source-less rules are attributed to a "Price source" that doesn't exist — `peg-alert-events.ts:230`: `evaluationCause` always calls `pegAlertSourceName`, which returns the literal `"Price source"` for an empty source (`peg-alert-copy.ts:47-49`), rendering "Grafana could not evaluate the Price source Peg rule" for the seven rules with `source = ""`

Canonical note now contradicts the code — `docs/notes/peg-monitoring.md:118` says "Slack titles use the severity icon plus that summary" but the summary is gone; `:132-133` says the backend "does not read Pending or canceled transitions" but it now reads Error transitions too

Monitoring-failure entries compete for the four visible slots — `route.ts:22`: `PEG_ALERTS_MAX_EVENTS = 4` and each error cycle emits two events, so one flapping datasource fills half the panel and two fill it entirely, pushing real peg breaches out of view
Response byte cap is now per-request — `route.ts:80`: `PEG_ALERTS_MAX_STATE_RESPONSE_BYTES` (4 MiB) is enforced inside the per-URL map, so a single `GET` can buffer up to 16 MiB instead of 8 MiB
Icon-only Slack title: the attachment title is what Slack shows in mobile push notifications and channel previews, so a page now previews as `🚨` with no cause — a real on-call ergonomics trade
